topic: The seven TRAPPIST-1 planets orbit at frequencies close to 24:15:9:6:4:3:2, a chain of three-body Laplace resonances that makes the whole system a single slow rhythm.
summary: TRAPPIST-1 is a cool red dwarf with seven Earth-sized planets, all found by their transits. Neighbouring period ratios are close to 8:5, 5:3, 3:2, 3:2, 4:3 and 3:2, and each set of three neighbours obeys a Laplace relation in which a weighted sum of their orbital longitudes stays nearly fixed. Scaled so planet h is 2, the orbital frequencies are almost exactly 24, 15, 9, 6, 4, 3 and 2. The chain links all seven planets and is thought to record their inward migration in the birth disk.

facts.claim: TRAPPIST-1 is an ultracool red dwarf of spectral type M8V about 40 light-years from the Sun.
Gillon and colleagues reported in 2017 that seven temperate Earth-sized planets transit the star.
facts.source_title: Gillon et al., Seven temperate terrestrial planets around the nearby ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1 (Nature 2017)

facts.claim: Luger and colleagues measured the outer planet h's period of about 18.77 days with K2 and showed the seven planets form a chain of three-body Laplace resonances.
facts.source_title: Luger et al., A seven-planet resonant chain in TRAPPIST-1 (arXiv:1703.04166)

facts.claim: Refined periods are 1.5108, 2.4219, 4.0492, 6.1010, 9.2075, 12.3524 and 18.7729 days for planets b to h.
facts.source_title: Agol et al., Refining the transit-timing and photometric analysis of TRAPPIST-1 (PSJ 2021)

facts.claim: Adjacent period ratios are close to 8:5, 5:3, 3:2, 3:2, 4:3 and 3:2 going outward from b to h.
The planets' masses were measured from transit-timing variations, the small shifts in transit times caused by their mutual pulls.
facts.source_title: Agol et al., Refining the transit-timing and photometric analysis of TRAPPIST-1 (PSJ 2021)

visualisable_mechanisms.name: Three-body Laplace resonance chain
visualisable_mechanisms.description: With orbital frequencies 24, 15, 9, 6, 4, 3, 2, combinations such as 2 lambda_b - 5 lambda_c + 3 lambda_d and lambda_f - 2 lambda_g + lambda_h have zero net rate, so the angles stay nearly fixed and the whole configuration repeats after h completes two orbits.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: Tune each planet's tone to its frequency ratio and sound it on every transit, so the resonance is heard as a polyrhythm that repeats as a whole.

visualisable_mechanisms.name: Synodic rose of a planet pair
visualisable_mechanisms.description: The chord joining two planets, drawn at regular intervals, traces a rose whose symmetry is set by the frequency difference divided by its common factor with the pair: three lobes for b and c, seven for d and h.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: Draw chords between pairs sampled back through time, fading with age.

visualisable_mechanisms.name: Conjunctions passing down the chain
visualisable_mechanisms.description: Neighbouring planets line up with the star at their synodic frequency; b and c meet about every 4 days, and conjunctions propagate outward along the chain.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: A gold ray and dyad at each neighbour conjunction, with a tidal ring from the star.

open_questions: How did the chain survive the star's early activity and the dispersal of its disk without breaking?
Do the planets keep thick atmospheres despite the strong flares of their star?

surprise.justification: Seven planets locked into one integer ratio chain is rare, and the ratios are simple enough to play as a chord.
